answer: The island multiplier is published, charged in tide, and grove lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 7 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 1505 identities would post 3390 proofs and burn roughly 49 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
